  has no ledger line and is named as such.
- The generator requires every selected raw directory to exist, reads every
  regular file in each directory, verifies lossless UTF-8, applies
  `redactSensitiveText`, requires redaction idempotence, and records both exact
  byte counts and SHA-256 hashes. A separate verifier reconstructs each payload
  from its markers and checks every recorded redacted byte count/hash against
  committed text, every original byte count/hash against the secured source,
  and one-to-one coverage for all source files and six JSONL lines.
- `ogz-meta/Alignment/OGZ-MASTER-ALIGNMENT.md:319` permits files over 1 MB with
  explicit intent. Trey explicitly ordered ruling 7a verbatim and explicitly
  tasked this mission to commit the redacted raw tapes inside the packet with
  dual hashes. That is specific operator intent for this packet's size, not a
  general waiver. Splitting, truncating, or omitting the tapes would violate the
  newer explicit task.

The exact independent verifier command and output were:

```text
$ NODE_PATH=/opt/ogzprime/OGZPMLV2/node_modules node - <<'NODE'
const crypto=require('crypto'),fs=require('fs');
const {redactSensitiveText}=require('./trai_brain/mercury-bridge/run-ledger');
const p='ogz-meta/inbox/codex/2026-08-29/record-the-rulings/EVIDENCE.md';
const text=fs.readFileSync(p,'utf8');
const sha=b=>crypto.createHash('sha256').update(b).digest('hex');
const re=/^### Tape (.+)\n\n- original_sha256: `([a-f0-9]{64})`\n- original_bytes: (\d+)\n- redacted_sha256: `([a-f0-9]{64})`\n- redacted_bytes: (\d+)\n- BEGIN REDACTED PAYLOAD \4\n([\s\S]*?)\n- END REDACTED PAYLOAD \4$/gm;
const found=new Map();let m;
while((m=re.exec(text))){
  const [_,source,oh,ob,rh,rb,capture]=m;
  if(found.has(source))throw new Error(`duplicate ${source}`);
  let payload=Buffer.from(capture,'utf8');
  if(payload.length+1===Number(rb))payload=Buffer.concat([payload,Buffer.from('\n')]);
  if(payload.length!==Number(rb)||sha(payload)!==rh)throw new Error(`redacted mismatch ${source}`);
  let original;
  if(/\.jsonl:\d+$/.test(source)){
    const [,file,line]=source.match(/^(.*\.jsonl):(\d+)$/);
    original=Buffer.from(fs.readFileSync(file,'utf8').split('\n')[Number(line)-1]+'\n','utf8');
  }else original=fs.readFileSync(source);
  if(original.length!==Number(ob)||sha(original)!==oh)throw new Error(`original mismatch ${source}`);
  if(Buffer.from(redactSensitiveText(original.toString('utf8')),'utf8').compare(payload)!==0)throw new Error(`redaction mismatch ${source}`);
  found.set(source,true);
}
const dirs=['2026-08-30t03-17-22-459z-1393195-23304fde33ea','2026-08-30t03-19-24-399z-1393800-07e2788ddce0','2026-08-30t08-08-16-572z-1415934-addb64d61844','2026-08-30t08-10-45-092z-1416706-e48bdebc61d3','2026-08-30t08-15-27-525z-1418086-a3a089239852','2026-08-30t08-23-18-166z-1420152-ee3b3efd741a','2026-08-30t08-28-24-646z-1421837-f569788b237b'];
const expected=[];
for(let i=1;i<=6;i++)expected.push(`ogz-meta/cognition-history/mercury-runs/2026-08-30.jsonl:${i}`);
for(const d of dirs){
  const root=`ogz-meta/cognition-history/mercury-runs/raw/2026-08-30/${d}`;
  for(const name of fs.readdirSync(root).sort()){
    const q=`${root}/${name}`;
    if(fs.statSync(q).isFile())expected.push(q);
  }
}
const missing=expected.filter(x=>!found.has(x));
const extra=[...found.keys()].filter(x=>!expected.includes(x));
if(missing.length||extra.length)throw new Error(JSON.stringify({missing,extra}));
const ledgerRunIds=fs.readFileSync('ogz-meta/cognition-history/mercury-runs/2026-08-30.jsonl','utf8').trim().split('\n').map(x=>JSON.parse(x).run_id);
console.log(JSON.stringify({redaction_idempotent:redactSensitiveText(text)===text,tapes_verified:found.size,expected_sources:expected.length,ledger_lines:ledgerRunIds.length,ledger_run_ids:ledgerRunIds,raw_directories:dirs.length,missing:missing.length,extra:extra.length},null,2));
NODE

    "2026-08-30T03-18-43-225Z-29e30b71ecbe",
    "2026-08-30T08-09-55-996Z-d918da4af05d",
    "2026-08-30T08-12-18-574Z-baadb3a9ad78",
```

## Named absences and limitations

- `mercury.ignore:19` excludes `inbox/`; Mercury model tools cannot open or
  diff this packet. Host-attested evidence was therefore required.
- `MISSION.md` itself is complete. Only host delivery of its lines 3 and 37 was
  omitted because the evidence-source redaction-invariance gate rejected those
  lines. They were never represented as reviewed.
- The first complete run did not review Part A; the interrupted attempt has no
  final ledger line; two later complete runs had empty Mercury diff scope. The
  broad final rerun was capped `UNVERIFIED`; the focused reconciliation remained
  `needs_more_evidence` until host tape and intent adjudication.
- Runs before ledger line 5 produced no quarantine or ntfy receipt. Ledger line
  5 records eight descriptor quarantines and successful max-priority ntfy
  receipts (HTTP 200). The dispatch rejection made no provider call. No runtime,
  broker, PM2, environment, or protected-path behavior was probed by this
  docs-only mission.

In the failure path (`openPosition` error) the trade is removed from the in‑memory map but **no `save()` is invoked**.  \n2. This violates the invariant that `activeTrades` “persists across restarts via save()/load()” (see StateManager constructor comment, line 521).  \n\n**Resulting failure mode**\n\n- After a failed order, a restart will reload the old `state.json` containing the now‑non‑existent trade, causing:\n  - Duplicate‑trade handling errors,\n  - Inconsistent position accounting,\n  - Potential double‑execution of the same order.\n\nThus the current fix (removing `this.save()` from `removeActiveTrade`) introduces a concrete break when the removal occurs without a subsequent `closePosition`. Execute on the trusted VPS runner in repository CGP-ME/OGZPMLV2, branch `codex/multi-asset-symbol-state`, preserving concurrent/unrelated work. One agent/box, strictly sequential Parts A→E. Full live adversarial layer per commit under current ladder/stamp rules; HOLD each push for genuine Fable cold-pull. No new env vars, config keys, defaults, or frameworks anywhere; sole exception Part E reads existing `NTFY_TOPIC` repo secret. Receipts must list inherited doctrine violations in every touched file. Never touch main. Do not create another thread.\n\nPART A — RECORD THE RULINGS (docs-only first commit).\nCreate `ogz-meta/inbox/trey/2026-08-29/RULINGS-2026-08-29.md` recording verbatim, attributed to Trey, dated:\n1. One net position per symbol — one trade per ticker at any time. Cross-frame conflicts resolve through the existing signal ranking; every declined frame writes a named refusal to the trace.\n2. Base timeframe = 1m. The base is received from the broker, never manufactured. All higher frames derive from it via TimeframeEngine per the MTF wire spec; Kraken native frames serve as validation.\n3. Account-level loss protection = TTP venue guards only. The six dead env caps are deleted, not rebuilt. Venue-guard translation through the bot must be proven (Part C audit + boot probe).\n4. Last price = the newest bar the broker sends, any frame; strategies only ever see the ruled frame architecture.\n5. ogz-meta/ledger is ruled contaminated as a class; per-file verdicts by Trey in progress; no deletion in this mission set.\n6. AuthFailureGuard demoted: no automation kills the bot, ever. Breach = broker-session quarantine + flatten + scream. Manual kill is the only stop.\n7. ACCOUNTABILITY PACKET (standing law). Every mission delivers one packet directory — ogz-meta/inbox/<agent>/<date>/<mission-slug>/ — as one commit, by the agent that did the work, into its own named directory, never another agent's. Contents: MISSION.md (tasking verbatim, dispatcher, ruling authority), WORK.md (commits produced, files touched), EVIDENCE.md (probes with commands + output, run IDs, tape hashes, named absences — what was NOT proven), REVIEW.md (adversarial panel as applied, attacks, adjudications, verdict), INHERITED.md (violations found in touched files, unfixed). A mission without its packet is not done. \"Pushed\" is not \"delivered.\" Code commits and packet cross-reference by SHA.\n7a. TAPES IN THE PACKET. EVIDENCE includes the raw adversarial tapes (ledger JSONL lines for the mission's runs + raw provider outputs), committed inside the packet — passed through redactSensitiveText before commit, with BOTH hashes recorded per file: original-on-box and redacted-as-committed. A tape that cannot be redacted safely is a named absence with its original hash — never a silent omission.\n8. VERDICT-SEAT FLOOR. The applied model is always stamped as fact. Verdict-bearing frames may be Fable or, via documented transition, Opus — never Sonnet, Haiku, or any lesser model. A verdict frame from below the floor is stamped identity_conflict and capped UNVERIFIED, run continues. Auxiliary/telemetry frames may be any model; recorded, no authority.\n9. PROTECTED-PATH ALARM — UNCONDITIONAL. Every push touching .env*, ecosystem.config.js, .claude/**, ogz-meta/Alignment/**, or config/trading.config.json fires max-priority ntfy naming author, SHA, files, and commit subject. No trailer logic, no exemptions, no approval concept, no blocking, no reverting — detection only. An alarm the operator stops reading is deleted, not tolerated.\nAlso record: protected-path screamer's TREY-APPROVED trailer design ruled out (detection value below noise floor); superseded by ruling 9.\n\nPART B — AUTHFAILUREGUARD DEMOTION.\nTerritory: `core/AuthFailureGuard.js` + its tests. Broker callers keep reporting failures unchanged. On threshold breach, replace `killSwitch.enableKillSwitch(reason)` with broker-session quarantine: halt entries for that broker's symbols, flatten that broker's open positions through the existing flatten path, mark the broker session quarantined (persists restart, operator-cleared only — same persistence discipline the KillSwitch flag uses), emit max-priority trace/ntfy with broker, kind, count, window, evidence. One net position per symbol — one trade per ticker at any time. Cross-frame conflicts resolve through the existing signal ranking; every declined frame writes a named refusal to the trace.\n2. The six dead env caps are deleted, not rebuilt. Venue-guard translation through the bot must be proven (Part C audit + boot probe).\n4. Last price = the newest bar the broker sends, any frame; strategies only ever see the ruled frame architecture.\n5. ogz-meta/ledger is ruled contaminated as a class; per-file verdicts by Trey in progress; no deletion in this mission set.\n6. AuthFailureGuard demoted: no automation kills the bot, ever. Breach = broker-session quarantine + flatten + scream. Manual kill is the only stop.\n7. ACCOUNTABILITY PACKET (standing law). Every mission delivers one packet directory — ogz-meta/inbox/<agent>/<date>/<mission-slug>/ — as one commit, by the agent that did the work, into its own named directory, never another agent's. Contents: MISSION.md (tasking verbatim, dispatcher, ruling authority), WORK.md (commits produced, files touched), EVIDENCE.md (probes with commands + output, run IDs, tape hashes, named absences — what was NOT proven), REVIEW.md (adversarial panel as applied, attacks, adjudications, verdict), INHERITED.md (violations found in touched files, unfixed). A mission without its packet is not done. \"Pushed\" is not \"delivered.\" Code commits and packet cross-reference by SHA.\n7a. TAPES IN THE PACKET. EVIDENCE includes the raw adversarial tapes (ledger JSONL lines for the mission's runs + raw provider outputs), committed inside the packet — passed through redactSensitiveText before commit, with BOTH hashes recorded per file: original-on-box and redacted-as-committed. A tape that cannot be redacted safely is a named absence with its original hash — never a silent omission.\n8. VERDICT-SEAT FLOOR. The applied model is always stamped as fact. On threshold breach, replace `killSwitch.enableKillSwitch(reason)` with broker-session quarantine: halt entries for that broker's symbols, flatten that broker's open positions through the existing flatten path, mark the broker session quarantined (persists restart, operator-cleared only — same persistence discipline the KillSwitch flag uses), emit max-priority trace/ntfy with broker, kind, count, window, evidence. The other broker is untouched. Remove the KillSwitch import from this file; KillSwitch itself remains, manual-only. Tests both directions: breach quarantines-flattens-screams and does NOT kill; the healthy broker keeps trading through the other's quarantine.\n\nPART C — GHOST CAPS OUT + VENUE-GUARD TRUTH.\nC1: delete every reference to `RISK_MANAGER_BYPASS`, `ACCOUNT_DRAWDOWN_BYPASS`, `MAX_DRAWDOWN`, `MAX_DAILY_LOSS`, `MAX_WEEKLY_LOSS`, `MAX_MONTHLY_LOSS` from env stamping surfaces within this agent's authority and from `config/.env.example`; correct any document (`ENV-VAR-AUDIT.md`) claiming these are HONORED — the claim is false; cite ruling 3 as authority. Runtime code should need no change (zero readers exist — verify, don't assume; if a reader is found, STOP and report, do not delete it).\nC2 (read-only, own inbox file): venue-guard chain audit. For every TTP venue-guard key in launch profiles: its runtime reader (file:line), breach action, how breach reaches entry-blocking, flatten, StateManager accounting, and trace. Gaps named, never inferred closed. Output `ogz-meta/inbox/<agent>/2026-08-29/venue-guard-chain-audit.md`. In the failure path (`openPosition` error) the trade is removed from the in‑memory map but **no `save()` is invoked**.  \n2. The comment in `removeActiveTrade` assumes a subsequent `closePosition()` will persist the change, but `closePosition()` is **not called** after a failed open.  \n3. Consequently the removal is lost on process restart or crash, leaving a stale trade in the persisted state. This violates the invariant that `activeTrades` “persists across restarts via save()/load()” (see StateManager constructor comment, line 521).  \n\n**Resulting failure mode**\n\n- After a failed order, a restart will reload the old `state.json` containing the now‑non‑existent trade, causing:\n  - Duplicate‑trade handling errors,\n  - Inconsistent position accounting,\n  - Potential double‑execution of the same order.\n\nThus the current fix (removing `this.save()` from `removeActiveTrade`) introduces a concrete break when the removal occurs without a subsequent `closePosition`. The break is provably present in the code paths shown above.","tool_calls":[],"tool_call_id":null},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":19199,"reasoning_tokens":197,"completion_tokens":607,"total_tokens":20003,"cached_input_tokens":6},"warning":null,"reasoning_summary":null}

{"id":"[REDACTED]","object":"chat.completion","created":1788077385,"model":"mercury-2","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"**Result:** The “concrete break” claimed in the previous answer does **not** exist for the current code.  \n\n**Why the claim fails**\n\n| Premise | Evidence |\n|---------|----------|\n| 1️⃣ `StateManager.openPosition()` can fail **before** any state‑update (and therefore before any `save()` call). | `openPosition()` returns early on identity, scope, or quantity validation failures (e.g., lines 1170‑1184 `return this._rejectOpenPositionIdentity…`, 1190‑1194 `return this._rejectOpenPositionScope…`, 1304‑1307 `return this._rejectOpenPositionQuantity…`). These returns happen **before** the lock is taken and before the call to `_applyStateUpdatesLocked`, which is the only place that triggers a `save()` (see lines 1057‑1059 in `_applyStateUpdatesLocked`). |\n| 2️⃣ When `OrderExecutor` receives a failed `positionResult` it calls `stateManager.removeActiveTrade(unifiedResult.orderId)` **without** persisting the state afterwards. | `OrderExecutor` failure path (lines 3999‑4015) shows the removal (`stateManager.removeActiveTrade(unifiedResult.orderId);`) followed immediately by a `return blockedReturn…`. No `stateManager.save()` or other persistence call follows this removal. |\n| 3️⃣ All `stateManager.save()` call sites are inside `_applyStateUpdatesLocked` (lines 1057‑1059) or other explicit update paths; none are invoked after the `removeActiveTrade` in the failure path. | `grep \"save(\" core/**/*.js` returns only the calls inside `_applyStateUpdatesLocked` (lines 759‑760, 1057‑1059, 2278‑2280, 4577‑4579) and the comment at line 2883. None of those are reachable after the `return` in the failure block of `OrderExecutor`. |\n| 4️⃣ A trade is only persisted when `openPosition()` succeeds and `_applyStateUpdatesLocked` runs, which includes a `save()` (see lines 1363‑1365 where the trade is added to `nextActiveTrades` and the final call `result = this._applyStateUpdatesLocked(updates, …)` at line 1390). | `StateManager.openPosition()` adds the trade to `nextActiveTrades` (line 1363) and then calls `_applyStateUpdatesLocked` (line 1390). `_applyStateUpdatesLocked` performs a `save()` (lines 1057‑1059). Therefore a trade is persisted **only** on a successful open. |\n| 5️⃣ If `openPosition()` fails, the trade is never added to `activeTrades` and never saved, so there is nothing to “lose” on restart. | The early‑return paths (Premise 1) prevent any addition to `activeTrades`. Consequently the `removeActiveTrade` call in the failure path operates on an empty map (no effect) and no persisted state is altered. |\n\n**Conclusion**\n\nThe failure path in `OrderExecutor` does **not** produce a stale trade on restart because:\n\n* The trade is never persisted when `openPosition()` fails (no `save()` occurs before the failure).\n* After the failure, `removeActiveTrade` is called without a subsequent `save()`, but there is nothing to remove from disk.\n* All `save()` calls happen inside `_applyStateUpdatesLocked`, which is only reached on successful state updates.\n\nTherefore the alleged “concrete break” is unsupported by the current code. The original verdict should be changed to **“NO CONCRETE BREAK FOUND.”**","tool_calls":[],"tool_call_id":null},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":27731,"reasoning_tokens":462,"completion_tokens":760,"total_tokens":28953,"cached_input_tokens":4433},"warning":null,"reasoning_summary":null}
